title: Prefix-group watermarks + access certificates for safe GPU KV eviction
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: As continuous batching and aggressive KV caching are used to reduce per-token cost, eviction decisions must be both memory-efficient and correct under concurrent inference pipelines. Current LRU+TTL heuristics occasionally evict prefix-affine entries that are still referenced by in-flight micro-batches, triggering degraded quality and rare OOMs when reclaimed memory is incorrectly reused. We need a correctness-first eviction policy that is prefix-aware, supports bounded TTL fallbacks, and provides strong invariants under sharded GPU allocation.
proposal: Introduce a prefix-group watermark and short-lived access certificates mechanism: (1) Group prefix-affine KV entries into prefix groups with a configurable soft-cap. (2) Maintain a per-group watermark indicating the lowest live sequence id whose KV may still be referenced by any active request. (3) Issue ephemeral access certificates to in-flight batches that pin sequence ranges; certificates carry a group+sequence tuple and expire on completion. (4) Eviction operates only on entries older than both the TTL and the group watermark and never reclaims data for which a certificate exists. For memory pressure emergencies, a controlled fallback proactively rejects new requests for affected prefixes and drains certificates before aggressive reclamation. The goal is deterministic safety (no use-after-free of KV slices) while preserving most batching-related cache hits.
design_decisions: 1) Use group watermarks rather than global LRU to avoid evicting frequently accessed tails of popular prefixes. 2) Certificates are lightweight 64-bit tokens issued by the scheduler to a batch and attached to all cache lookups; tokens are removed on batch completion. 3) Watermark monotonicity is enforced via atomic compare-and-swap on the group control block to work across shards. 4) TTL remains as a secondary eviction signal to bound long-tail growth; TTL < 30m by default. 5) Fencing: eviction worker must consult the group certificate bitmap before freeing GPU pages; if any certificate overlaps, eviction defers or promotes to background reclamation with copying to host memory if necessary.
implementation_plan:
- Phase 1 (tech spike): implement group metadata (in CPU memory) and a certificate allocator; add unit tests for issuance/return semantics. GitHub spike branch: runtime/spike/prefix-cert. (2w)
- Phase 2: add atomic watermark CAS and integrate with shard-level eviction worker; implement consult path that is O(1) for common case (no certificates). Add fuzz harness to exercise races. PR: runtime/pull/2194. (3w)
- Phase 3: GPU integration: ensure page freeing goes through the fencing check; add emergency reclaim path with request throttling. End-to-end perf + correctness tests. PR: runtime/pull/2238. (2w)
- Phase 4: Canary rollout (5% traffic), monitor metrics, iterate on watermark thresholds and TTL. (1w)
acceptance_criteria:
- No cache use-after-free seen in the fuzz harness across 100k randomized runs.
- Integration e2e runs pass with synthetic continuous-batching workload at 90th percentile latency < baseline+10% and memory reclaimed within target window.
- Canary for 5% production traffic shows <0.1% increase in 500/5xx errors and no OOM incidents.
- Unit tests cover certificate lifecycle, watermark CAS races, and emergency reclaim path.
tests:
- Unit tests for certificate allocator and group watermark CAS.
- Deterministic race tests that simulate certificate issuance during eviction.
- Fuzz tests (100k runs) to try to provoke use-after-free between eviction and batch completion.
- GPU OOM simulation harness that forces page reclamation under concurrent batches.
- Performance benchmark comparing cache hit rate and latency against existing LRU+TTL baseline.
observability: New metrics: prefix_group_watermark_age_seconds, active_prefix_certificates_total, eviction_deferrals_total, emergency_reclaims_total. Traces: certificate.issue, certificate.return, eviction.check, eviction.free. Dashboard: runtime -> KV Cache -> Prefix Certificates. Alert: emergency_reclaims_total > 10 in 5m -> page through oncall runbook.
rollout_plan:
- Merge behind feature flag 'prefix_certificate_eviction'.
- Canary 5% for 72h with tight monitoring on OOMs, 5xx, and cache hit rate.
- If stable, ramp to 25% for 48h, then 100% with staged config tuning (soft caps per prefix group).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Certificate bookkeeping might add latency to hot-path lookups. Mitigation: keep certificate check fast-path inlined and only consult bitmap on eviction path; measure p50/p95. Risk: Watermark CAS contention on hotspots. Mitigation: sharded group metadata and backoff on CAS failures. Risk: Emergency reclaim may block throughput. Mitigation: fallback policy to reject new requests for affected prefixes and provide graceful degradation messaging.
notes:
- Chose certificates over reference counting because refcounts across shards were causing scalability bottlenecks in earlier experiments.
- TTL configured per-customer via their Dedicated/Private policy to limit cross-tenant memory exposure.
- This approach is compatible with existing prefix pinning heuristics used by the prefetcher.
